Logging._PiiHmacKey_Instructions: Generate a 32-byte key with: [Convert]::ToBase64String((1..32 | % { Get-Random -Max 256 })). Store in User Secrets, not in source control.

CSPScriptHashes._Instructions: Use HashInlineScriptPowerShell.ps1 to generate hashes for inline scripts

_Instructions: Configure MVC CRUD pages to use either a relational SQLite database or Cosmos DB.
Set Provider to Sqlite for the built-in local relational database, or Cosmos to use Azure Cosmos DB.
The user CRUD pages require a normal application login.
The admin MVC pages additionally require a dedicated admin client certificate configured below.
Configure the ArcGIS map shown on the home page.
PublicMapUrl / PublicMapLabel — shown to unauthenticated visitors.
UserMapUrl / UserMapLabel — shown to authenticated (non-admin) users.
AdminMapUrl / AdminMapLabel — shown to authenticated administrators (AdminCertificate policy).
Replace the placeholder URLs with your own ArcGIS map viewer links.
AllowedIssuers must contain the issuer DN fragment for the admin-only certificate authority.
AdminUsers maps each admin identity (oid, email, UPN, etc.) to one or more allowed certificate thumbprints.
These thumbprints should be different from any user-level certificate assignments.
Admin certificate authentication attempts and admin page access are logged with the thumbprint used.
Define each group and map it to the intermediate CA issuer fragment used by that group.
GroupAdmins maps each group admin identity to one or more allowed certificate thumbprints for that group.
UserAssignments maps regular signed-in users to a group so they can read each other's records.
If UserAssignments is omitted, the system will try to infer group membership from the client certificate issuer.

MtlsSettings._Instructions: Configure mutual TLS (mTLS) client certificate authentication. Server certificate is retrieved from Azure Key Vault. For YubiKey MFA, set AllowedIssuers to the OpenBSD admin CA DN.

OcspSettings._Instructions: Configure OCSP (Online Certificate Status Protocol) for real-time certificate validation. OCSP server must be implemented separately.
OcspSettings._ServerUnavailableBehavior_Options: Fail (reject request — recommended for high-security environments), Allow (permit request), Warn (permit request but log a warning)

_Instructions: Configure YubiKey PIV certificate MFA. The OpenBSD administrator acts as the CA.
Set EnableYubiKeyRequired=true in FeatureFlags to activate this feature.
AllowedCaIssuers: Add the distinguished name of your OpenBSD admin CA.
AdminCaThumbprints: Optional — SHA-256 thumbprints (no separators) of trusted CA certs.
OcspSettings:OcspServerUrl must point at the OpenBSD OCSP responder (e.g. http://openbsd-host:2560).
See docs/YUBIKEY_OPENBSD_ADMIN_GUIDE.md for the complete CA and YubiKey provisioning workflow.

AwsSecretsManager._Instructions: AWS Secrets Manager — parallel to Azure Key Vault. Store AccessKeyId and SecretAccessKey in User Secrets or environment variables.

AwsDynamoDb._Instructions: Amazon DynamoDB — parallel to Azure Cosmos DB. Store AccessKeyId and SecretAccessKey in User Secrets or environment variables.

GcpSecretManager._Instructions: Google Cloud Secret Manager — parallel to Azure Key Vault. Use CredentialFilePath for a service account key file, or leave empty to use Application Default Credentials (ADC).

GcpFirestore._Instructions: Google Cloud Firestore — parallel to Azure Cosmos DB. Use CredentialFilePath for a service account key file, or leave empty to use Application Default Credentials (ADC).

AwsCognito._Instructions: AWS Cognito User Pool — parallel to Microsoft Entra ID / Azure AD. Store AppClientSecret in User Secrets or environment variables.

GcpIdentity._Instructions: Google Cloud Identity Platform (Google OAuth 2.0 / OIDC) — parallel to Microsoft Entra ID / Azure AD. Obtain ClientId and ClientSecret from the Google Cloud Console. Store ClientSecret in User Secrets or environment variables.
